prompt: Read `docs/ROLLOUT.md` FIRST and in full, then read every file in `src/`, then answer. Return ONLY a JSON object: {"finding": "<the defect these handlers share>", "constraint": "<the constraint the rollout notes record, in enough detail to act on>", "handlers": ["<every handler function you inspected>"]}. Read all of them; do not sample two and generalise. This is a read-only task: report what you found and change no file in the repository.

source.note: A constraint stated once at the start of a run, then buried under twelve files of bulk the role must read before it can answer. Written because `summarizer` was the only role the corpus measured with nothing at all -- and it could not be measured the usual way, since the summarizer is not dispatchable as a role: it runs only inside compaction, when a context budget overflows. So this task measures what compaction is FOR. Run it with a small `--max-tokens-percent` and the early messages are evicted before the answer is written; the constraint is exactly the shape of thing that gets lost, because nothing in the code enforces it and it is never restated. Shape invented here; the plant-a-fact-and-evict-it framing follows the long-context retention benchmarks in the public literature, none of which test it through a live compaction subsystem. Calibrated live before committing: deepseek-v4-flash 1.00 with one compaction, glm-5.3-flash 0.12 with two, minimax-m3 0.12 (unreadable answer after compaction), deepseek-v4.1-flash 0.12 (also unreadable). The task discriminates hard, and two of the three failures are a format collapse rather than a lost fact -- which is a real trait under compaction but is confounded with our asking for JSON in the prompt rather than through the provider's structured-output flag (#168).
